description: Paktai Geo brings together geospatial analysis, machine learning and socioeconomic research in Quito. For Dancing with the SARs, we plan to explore NISAR surface-change observations and communicate them through an accessible interactive map. We welcome radar remote sensing, GIS, data validation and web skills. Spanish and English are welcome. Existing flood research is background experience; challenge-specific work will begin during the hackathon.
summary: Quito in radar is a PAKTAI Geo companion for Dancing with the SARs. It compares NASA–ISRO NISAR imagery from 7 and 19 October 2026 over the same part of Quito. The prototype lets users move a slider across the two dates and inspect a selected point in the existing PAKTAI Geo atlas. It also prepares a coordinate-specific query for a compatible AI assistant connected to PAKTAI Geo via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The connector can retrieve rainfall alerts, terrain-based flood susceptibility and census context with source dates and limitations. The comparison supports visual screening for possible surface changes, which require independent verification. The atlas and MCP connector predate the hackathon.
details:
Hackathon work

We built a standalone HTML, CSS and JavaScript comparison of two NISAR L-band Level 2 GCOV false-color views for Quito. The imagery comes from NASA EOSDIS GIBS. Two provisional CMR records match descending track 112, frame 089 and the same processing configuration on 7 and 19 October 2026. We queried the same geographic extent for both dates. The slider reveals differences in rendered radar backscatter. A click or coordinate entry opens the corresponding point in the existing atlas and prepares an AI query for that location. The false-color comparison is qualitative. Differences can reflect moisture, roughness, vegetation or processing and need independent observations before attributing a cause.

Existing PAKTAI Geo capabilities

The public atlas combines terrain, weather, census and business-location context. A read-only MCP connector allows compatible clients such as Claude or ChatGPT to call six tools: point climate and three-day forecast, parish rainfall alerts and satellite observations when available, 2022 census profiles at 500 m, 1 km and 3 km, flood susceptibility in Quito, Quito business-opening simulations, and climate exposure by sector for up to 50 locations. Parish alerts and census profiles cover Quito, Guayaquil, Cuenca, Santo Domingo and Portoviejo. Point climate covers continental Ecuador. The Quito susceptibility rank is relative, while the business simulation estimates potential. Neither gives expected losses or sales.

Verified example

On 15 November the six MCP tools responded at -0.2030, -78.4900. The response identified Mariscal Sucre, placed the cell at 74.58 out of 100 in relative flood susceptibility and estimated 15,309 residents within 1 km using the 2022 Census. Weather results are time-dependent. The atlas and MCP connector predate the 2026 event. The submission includes the event-specific prototype and a five-slide demonstration. OpenAI Codex assisted with source review, coding, writing and preparation of the presentation. The radar imagery comes from NASA GIBS.
